The configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶ corresponds to a total of 10 electrons, which is the electron configuration of neon (Ne), a noble gas. 1. Cl⁻: Chlorine (Cl) has an atomic number of 17, so it has 17 electrons in its neutral state. Adding an electron for Cl⁻ gives it a total of 18 electrons. Its configuration becomes 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶.

2. F⁻: Fluorine (F) has an atomic number of 9, so it has 9 electrons in its neutral state. Adding an electron for F⁻ gives it a total of 10 electrons. Its configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶.

3. Na⁺: Sodium (Na) has an atomic number of 11, so it has 11 electrons in its neutral state. Losing an electron for Na⁺ gives it a total of 10 electrons. Its configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶.

4. Ne: Neon (Ne) naturally has 10 electrons, with the configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶.
